title: Assessment of Optimum Renewable Energy System for the Somalia–Turkish Training and Research Hospital in Mogadishu
venue_or_publisher: Journal of Renewable Energy and Environment 8(3), 54–67
data_period: Hospital load: 2017–2018; wind reference: 2015–2017; cost vintage unclear.
method: HOMER hybrid-system optimization using a historical hospital load profile.
data_sources: Technical-department load measurements; NASA weather inputs and synthesized hourly solar resource.
key_findings: The model selects a wind/diesel/battery configuration at a simulated USD 0.191/kWh.
limitations: One site; raw series not obtained and public download not identified. Wind measurement wording conflicts with its NASA citation; Fig.2 power/energy labels require care.
project_relevance: Obtain and validate the hospital’s original hourly load series.
evidence_type: techno-economic simulation with reported measured load
verification_locator: Sections 2.2–2.3, Fig. 2 (printed p.56/PDF p.3), optimization and conclusion; institutional metadata also checked.
quality_appraisal: Useful measured-load provenance; modeled optimum is not installed-system performance.
data_code_availability: No downloadable raw load series or HOMER project identified.

title: Economics, environmental foot print and sustainability of community scale solar desalination plant in water scarce Somalia coastal regions
data_period: Input weather/cost years not verifiable from accessible abstract.
method: Community desalination design and economic/environmental simulation.
data_sources: Abstract describes local water and energy inputs; underlying datasets not inspected.
key_findings: A modeled 3 m³/day plant yields location-dependent water costs of USD 8.66–9.48/m³.
limitations: Paywalled methods. A published correction exists; its substantive text was inaccessible.
project_relevance: Useful desalination design lead after checking corrected assumptions and brine constraints.
verification_locator: Publisher abstract and metadata; correction https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10098-024-02797-z (23 March 2024).
quality_appraisal: Scenario evidence only; do not calibrate with abstract numbers before resolving the correction.
data_code_availability: Publisher lists data available on request; no public model identified.

title: Analyzing the Economic Viability and Design of Solar-Powered Water Pumps for Farming Irrigation: Case Study Conducted in Somalia
venue_or_publisher: Forthcoming Networks and Sustainability in the AIoT Era, LNNS 1036, 1–13
geographic_scope: Banana farm in southern Somalia; precise location absent from abstract
data_period: Input and field dates not reported in accessible abstract.
method: CROPWAT water-requirement calculations and PVSYST pumping simulations.
data_sources: Crop needs and solar-system assumptions; original inputs not inspected.
key_findings: For an 82 m³/day duty, modeled DC pumping costs less than AC and diesel alternatives.
limitations: Head, cost-year, discounting and water-resource assumptions inaccessible; no measured operating comparison established.
project_relevance: Pumping methods and comparator design; obtain complete assumptions before reuse.
verification_locator: Publisher abstract, author list, publication date and reference list; online 26 June 2024.
quality_appraisal: Conditional farm design, unsuitable as a national pumping-cost parameter.

title: Feasibility Study on Solar PV Irrigation and Freezer Systems in Puntland, Somalia: Harnessing Sunshine, Powering Somalia
data_period: 2024 survey; report December 2024, landing page April 2025.
method: Farmer/fishmonger surveys, interviews and system-cost feasibility assessment.
key_findings: Identifies irrigation and freezing demand, financing constraints and proposed payment mechanisms.
limitations: Farm areas change from m² to hectares between pp.27 and 30; Bari chart components do not sum to its total.
project_relevance: Questionnaire/site leads; quarantine quantitative inputs pending original-data reconciliation.
verification_locator: Methods p.8; survey pp.26–31; freezer discussion pp.63–65. PDF pp.28 and 31 visually checked.
quality_appraisal: Direct local research, but substantial internal consistency problems prevent unqualified numerical reuse.
data_code_availability: No respondent-level data or reproducible model located.

title: Technical Report: Somalia: Groundwater Assessment
geographic_scope: Somalia, with subnational aquifer and water-point distinctions
data_period: SWALIM water-point information through 2020; historical studies and 2017–2019 cost references.
method: Hydrogeological synthesis and illustrative water-supply cost comparisons.
data_sources: SWALIM, earlier groundwater studies, and international pumping-cost references.
key_findings: Aquifer depth, salinity and sustainable abstraction constrain solar pumping and desalination options.
limitations: Illustrative solar/diesel costs partly originate outside Somalia; inventory coverage varies.
project_relevance: Link energy-system sizing to water availability and treatment requirements.
evidence_type: technical review with secondary geospatial data
verification_locator: Title/credits, summary, solar/desalination discussion p.41 and Appendix 7, pp.78–80.
quality_appraisal: Strong water-resource context; cost examples are not a representative Somali price survey.
data_code_availability: SWALIM water-point inventory is a data lead; no analysis-ready extraction acquired.

title: Women’s small-scale fisheries organizations in Jubaland State of Somalia
geographic_scope: Surveyed Jubaland fishing organizations; Jamame access restricted
data_period: Main survey 21 December 2022–25 January 2023; follow-ups January/March 2023; publication March 2024.
method: Purposive organizational survey and follow-up interviews.
data_sources: Twenty-one groups and five individual vendors; stakeholder interviews.
key_findings: Storage, transport and finance constrain women’s fish businesses; one cited ice facility had battery-related downtime.
limitations: Security and organizational sampling limit coverage; no metered cold-chain energy data.
project_relevance: Design gender-aware cold-chain demand and maintenance fieldwork.
verification_locator: Methods pp.8–10; storage/market findings; p.31 footnote 7 on Alanley ice-machine operation.
quality_appraisal: Valuable primary local evidence, not national prevalence or a current facility census.
data_code_availability: Survey instrument described; public respondent microdata not identified.

title: Final Report: Conducting Fish Price Assessment (Baseline) in the Federal Republic of Somalia & Federal Member States
venue_or_publisher: Ministry of Fisheries and Blue Economy, Federal Republic of Somalia
geographic_scope: Banadir, Puntland, Galmudug, South West, Jubaland and Hirshabelle
method: Questionnaires, key-informant interviews and focus groups.
data_sources: 673 respondents across six regional strata; fish prices, costs and market conditions.
key_findings: Documents cold-chain constraints and recommends solar ice/cold-storage investment.
limitations: Seasonal baseline, not impact evaluation. Female participation prose conflicts with Table 4 for Hirshabelle.
project_relevance: Useful value-chain questionnaire and cost variables; reconcile tables before quantitative reuse.
verification_locator: Methods pp.11–14; Table 4 (p.13/PDF p.18, visually checked); Table 8; recommendations pp.52–53.
quality_appraisal: Primary government-hosted baseline with material internal inconsistency; recommendations do not prove energy-investment returns.
data_code_availability: Questionnaire annex available; microdata not linked. Public URL bears an Official Use Only marking; PDF not redistributed.

title: Environmental and Financial Impacts of Electrification of Healthcare Facilities in Selected Humanitarian Settings
venue_or_publisher: Global Platform for Action Coordination Unit / UNITAR, with NORCAP and WHO-hosted HEPA
geographic_scope: Multi-country brief with a Somalia case covering 49 healthcare facilities
data_period: September 2025 publication; Somalia assessment dates not specified.
method: Needs-assessment synthesis and standardized solar/diesel cost scenarios.
data_sources: WHO facility assessments; standard health-service profiles; supplier and installation cost experience.
key_findings: Identifies Somali facilities requiring electrification or rehabilitation and budgets solar provision.
limitations: Standardized 18.4 kWh/day PHC profile is not metered site demand; multi-country headcount totals are internally inconsistent.
project_relevance: Locate the original 49 assessments and distinguish essential services from assumed loads.
verification_locator: Somalia case p.2; Table 1 p.3 (PDF p.4, visually checked); assumptions and cost appendices.
quality_appraisal: Useful facility-assessment lead; aggregate totals and transferred costs need reconciliation.
data_code_availability: No public site-level hourly profiles or cost workbook identified.

title: Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) for the Education Facilities in Northeastern State of Somalia
authors: Federal Republic of Somalia, Ministry of Energy and Water Resources, SESRP Project Implementation Unit
venue_or_publisher: Ministry of Energy and Water Resources
geographic_scope: Named education facilities in Northeastern State, using the report’s administrative label
data_period: Site surveys September–October 2024; consultations 7–13 April 2025; final November 2025.
method: Site reconnaissance, proposed PV-system planning and environmental/social assessment.
key_findings: Provides a concrete institutional solar pipeline and location-specific implementation constraints.
limitations: Plans and estimated requirements establish neither commissioning nor education outcomes.
project_relevance: Locate the referenced Data Collection and Assessment Report and verify load definitions.
verification_locator: Cover; sections 1–2, Tables 1-1 and 2-1; consultation section 4.
quality_appraisal: Primary site/planning evidence; capacity proposals must remain separate from observed demand.
data_code_availability: Facility tables public; underlying assessment/load files not obtained.

title: World Bank Enterprise Survey 2025: Somalia
geographic_scope: Eligible registered private firms with at least five workers; excludes informal microfirms and primary agriculture
method: Stratified enterprise survey by industry, size and region.
data_sources: 2024 Somali business-census frame and firm questionnaires.
key_findings: Includes self-reported monthly electricity consumption; variable c32 has 241 nonmissing observations.
limitations: Use survey weights; missingness and sector exclusions preclude an all-business national demand estimate.
project_relevance: Analyze firm energy consumption alongside service constraints and business characteristics.
quality_appraisal: High-value documented survey; no weighted estimates computed in this review.
data_code_availability: Microdata catalog and questionnaires identified; data access not exercised.

title: Nexus between renewable energy and agricultural productivity in Somalia: Evidence from Fragile Foundations
method: ARDL time-series association with FMOLS robustness checks.
data_sources: World Bank renewable share of total final energy; SESRIC agricultural value-added growth and macroeconomic series.
key_findings: Reports a positive long-run energy-share association; short-run renewable term is not statistically significant.
limitations: Small annual sample; aggregate energy share is not solar-pump adoption. Agricultural value-added growth is not farm yield.
project_relevance: Motivates disaggregated exposure and outcome measures, not causal technology returns.
verification_locator: Publisher-distributed full text on ResearchGate: section 3.1/Table 1, results Tables 3–7, data statement; Crossref metadata.
quality_appraisal: Traceable variables, but causal and technology-specific interpretations exceed the design.
data_code_availability: Processed data available on author request; public replication package not identified.

title: Building resilient food systems in Somalia: Integrated approaches for conflict and climate challenges
geographic_scope: NCA programming in Puntland and Jubaland
data_period: Main monitoring/cases 2022–2024 within a longer organizational history; online August 2025, later version October 2025.
method: Program monitoring synthesis and 18 purposive qualitative case studies.
data_sources: Monitoring of 2,200 smallholders; interviews, focus groups and organizational reports.
key_findings: Reports gains from bundled agriculture, solar irrigation, training and cooperative interventions.
limitations: Implementer evidence lacks a clearly identified solar-only counterfactual; access and selection constrain generalization.
project_relevance: Study ownership, maintenance, market access and water management alongside electricity.
verification_locator: Current publisher HTML: Research scope and methodology; Results; Challenges. Version history and references checked.
quality_appraisal: Useful implementation evidence; reported yield gains cannot be assigned to solar alone.
data_code_availability: No public underlying monitoring dataset identified; cited final evaluation remains a retrieval lead.

title: UNICEF Somalia – Final evaluation of “Improving children’s access to water and sanitation in Somalia (2015–2018)”
venue_or_publisher: MDF Training & Consultancy and Polaris Global Management for UNICEF
geographic_scope: Project locations in Awdal, Bari, Galgaduud and Lower Juba
data_period: Project 2015–2018; evaluation published April 2019; exact interview dates not resolved.
method: Triangulated interviews, community discussions, household survey, observation and contribution analysis.
data_sources: Project monitoring, beneficiaries, implementing partners and facility visits.
key_findings: Solar pumping supported lower operating costs, while supply, spares and installation quality complicated delivery.
limitations: Project-location survey is not statistically generalizable; bundled WASH intervention does not isolate a solar effect.
project_relevance: Build maintenance, procurement and service continuity into productive-energy research.
verification_locator: Methods pp.33–41; relevance/effectiveness pp.43–58; efficiency/sustainability pp.61–70; recommendations pp.75–76.
quality_appraisal: Strong triangulation for operational lessons; historical, project-specific outcomes.
data_code_availability: Instruments/respondent categories in annexes; raw responses not publicly linked.

title: The investment case for sustainable water systems in Somalia
geographic_scope: Somali water-supply illustrations and a hypothetical 10,000-person service area
method: Four-year cost comparison of trucking, rehabilitation, new supply and blended strategies.
data_sources: UNICEF WASH costing tool; Somali price and system-cost examples.
key_findings: Rehabilitation is cheapest under the brief’s assumed service and financing conditions.
limitations: Scenarios combine diesel deep wells and solar shallow wells; subsidy/inflation assumptions drive comparisons.
project_relevance: Useful service-cost framework, not a pure solar-versus-diesel estimate.
verification_locator: All five PDF pages; assumptions p.3 and cost table p.4.
quality_appraisal: Transparent headline assumptions; modeled savings are not observed investment returns.
data_code_availability: Summary inputs public; underlying workbook not identified.

title: Technical Support to Village Milk Collection Centres in North Somalia
venue_or_publisher: VSF-Germany, EDF-9 Somali Pastoral Dairy Development Project Phase II
geographic_scope: Togdheer/western Sool and Nugal/Sanaag/Bari, preserving report-specific Somaliland/Puntland labels
data_period: November–December 2012 fieldwork; report 21 December 2012; author upload 2016.
method: Visits to 20 of 25 collection centres plus telephone/staff assessments.
data_sources: Centre inspection and interviews with managers and milk-market participants.
key_findings: Access, water, ownership and unfinished facilities constrained use; solar cooling was proposed.
limitations: Historical qualitative assessment; no measured refrigeration energy or demonstrated solar-cooling impact.
project_relevance: Locate centres and compare equipment provision with actual service uptake.
verification_locator: Author-uploaded original report: executive summary pp.2–5 and centre assessments. Repository DOI is not peer-review certification.
quality_appraisal: Useful dairy field evidence, not a current national cold-chain inventory.
data_code_availability: Centre tables included; no machine-readable energy measurements identified.

title: Solar versus Diesel Powered Water Pumps in Meeting Sustainability Goals in Somalia, a qualitative study
data_period: Posted July 2026; interview dates not clearly reported.
method: Purposive interviews with ten key informants; thematic template analysis in NVivo.
key_findings: Stakeholders identify finance, skills, theft, weak policy and limited community inclusion as barriers.
limitations: Providers dominate the sample; water users and marginalized groups are missing. No financial or energy-performance comparison.
project_relevance: Develop inclusive maintenance/ownership questions for future water-service fieldwork.
verification_locator: Cover preprint/data statements; methods sections 2.3–2.6; findings and limitations.
quality_appraisal: Exploratory stakeholder evidence; explicitly not submitted to a peer-reviewed journal at posting.
data_code_availability: Anonymized qualitative data may be available from corresponding author on reasonable request, subject to ethical/confidentiality restrictions; no data received.
bibliographic_note: Primary PDF cover orders authors Kassa, Elema, Redding; EarthArXiv/Crossref order Kassa, Redding, Elema. Catalogue retains the inspected PDF order; discrepancy is explicit.

title: Development and implementation of a cost-effective automated irrigation system for resource-constrained environments: a case study of Mogadishu, Somalia
data_period: Thirty-day experiment; exact field dates unresolved; publication 2 July 2026.
method: Automated sensor-controlled versus manual irrigation prototype comparison.
data_sources: One-square-metre plots; water and labour observations.
key_findings: Reports water and labour savings using a grid-powered prototype.
limitations: Short, tiny-plot experiment; no rural off-grid validation or metered energy-saving result established.
project_relevance: Demand-control research lead; do not transfer water-saving percentages directly to national pumping energy.
verification_locator: Publisher-distributed full text on ResearchGate: methods, results and data statement; Crossref publication metadata.
quality_appraisal: Useful proof of concept; seasonal durability, scaling and energy benefits remain unverified.
data_code_availability: Data available on request; no public replication dataset identified.

title: Techno-economic and environmental analysis of a fully renewable hybrid energy system for sustainable power infrastructure advancement
data_period: Published 9 April 2025; resource and load observation years not specified in inspected sections.
method: HOMER configuration optimization; MATLAB plotting; economic/environmental calculations.
data_sources: NASA POWER weather; scaled demand of 2,042.70 kWh/day; assumed PHES reservoir 1,000 m³, head 100 m and storage 245 kWh.
key_findings: PV/wind/PHES ranks cheapest in simulation; reported USD 0.03845/kWh and 0.31-year payback are unvalidated projections.
limitations: Metered demand provenance unclear. Authors defer site-specific elevation validation; reservoir civil works and storage-autonomy consistency need audit.
verification_locator: Publisher HTML: location/load; PHES; economic equations 14–18; weather; results/autonomy; data/code statements. Table 2 linked view did not resolve independently.
quality_appraisal: Conceptual design, not measured port operation or proven local PHES feasibility.
data_code_availability: Data on reasonable request; MATLAB plotting code on request; public HOMER project not identified.
